slides.title: Share Your Views
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 5 English, Unit 8: Share Your Views. Unit 8 is about persuasion: how people share a view and try to bring others with them. You read a school campaign poster, learn to separate a fact that can be proved from an opinion that somebody holds, and take apart the persuasive toolkit of rhetorical questions, emotive language, expert opinion and calls to action. Twenty-five words carry the unit, from evidence and judicial to physiology and hemisphere. Six grammar lessons cover the present perfect with for and since, adverbs of degree with comparatives and superlatives, adjective order, similes, and sequencing words with modal verbs. In the story, Amal and Nora investigate an ancient hall that stands without steps, and prove that a careful question beats a repeated legend. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Read persuasive posters, information texts and narrative, and identify how each one presents a viewpoint.
Distinguish a fact that can be proved from an opinion that somebody merely holds.
Use adverbs of degree, comparative adjectives and superlative adjectives to strengthen a claim.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read persuasive posters, information texts and narrative, and identify how each one presents a viewpoint. You will also distinguish a fact that can be proved from an opinion that somebody merely holds. You will also use adverbs of degree, comparative adjectives and superlative adjectives to strengthen a claim. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: intelligence, citizenship, physician, geographer, ancient, magnificent. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Fact, Opinion and the Persuasive Toolkit
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Save Our School Garden! and Fact, Opinion and the Persuasive Toolkit. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: The Present Perfect Tense
bullets: The present perfect ties a past action to the present moment. We build it from have or has plus a past participle. Use it for experiences, achievements...
slides.narration: The first language focus is The Present Perfect Tense. The present perfect ties a past action to the present moment. We build it from have or has plus a past participle. Use it for experiences, achievements and situations that are still going on. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: One Minute to Persuade. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
